items.title: Manuel Joseph "Moose" Zanco Interview, 1959-11-25
items.q: I had one fella tell me that during the war that, uh, Hitler outlawed, uh, jazz.

ctx.x: Well, who, who did you hear over there? Did you listen to any bands on your way back?

Uh, well, we just, uh, had the opportunity to catch, uh, De Parry's band in New York, but over there, I mean, uh, uh, all the groups that were sent over there were all modern jazz groups. We were the only, uh, Dixieland group, you know, on this tour, see. Everything else was, uh, modern jazz. Most of the, uh, people from over there, the Austrians themselves, they, they have bands in the different nightclubs and all, and they all play modern jazz. So, uh, to hear Dixieland was something different for them, you…
Where was this, at Vienna, that area you played in, castles? Yeah, mm-hmm.
